note: Relay received syslog, SNMP traps and flow exports on to external collectors, or stream them into BigQuery as queryable rows. Core does the sending, so only one egress point has to be allowed through a firewall.
unavailable: Managing forwarding requires the admin role.
signInPrompt: Sign in to manage forwarding destinations.
empty: No forwarding destinations yet. Nothing is being relayed.
securityNote: Forwarded messages leave Yagra. Syslog bodies routinely carry credentials — send them only to a collector you trust, over a network you trust.

delete.title: Delete destination
delete.confirm: Delete "{{name}}"? Nothing further will be forwarded to it.

field.name: Name
field.targetHint: host:port. Use [address]:port for a literal IPv6 address.
field.targetTableHint: project.dataset.table. The dataset must already exist — Yagra will not create one, because a dataset's region cannot be changed afterwards. The table is created automatically, partitioned by day.
field.fidelityHint: Original relays the datagram exactly as received. Rebuilt regenerates it from the parsed fields, which loses RFC 5424 structured data, non-UTF-8 bytes, text past 4096 characters, and varbinds past the 32nd.
field.fidelityImpossible: This pairing cannot carry the original bytes, so the message is always rebuilt.
field.fidelityVerbatimOnly: A flow export is a template plus many records in one binary datagram, so it can only be relayed exactly as received.
field.fidelityRowsOnly: BigQuery receives normalized rows — one per event, one per flow record — with typed columns. The original bytes are deliberately not stored: a raw-payload column would make anything sensitive in a log line permanently queryable off-box.
field.serviceAccountPlaceholder: Leave empty to use the instance's own identity (Workload Identity)
field.serviceAccountKept: a key is stored — leave empty to keep it
field.serviceAccountHint: Paste the JSON key file for a service account with the BigQuery Data Editor role. It is encrypted at rest and never shown again. Leave it empty when core runs on Google Cloud with Workload Identity — that stores no credential at all and is the better option.
field.caCertHint: Optional. Paste the PEM certificate of the CA that signed the collector, if it is not in the system trust store. The collector's certificate is always verified — there is no way to turn that off.
field.communityHint: Used only when a trap has to be rebuilt. A relayed original carries the device's own community.
field.rateLimitHint: Messages per second. Excess is dropped and counted, never queued.

filter.label: Filter
filter.emptyHint: No conditions — the whole stream is forwarded.
filter.flowAnyRecord: A flow datagram carries many records at once. If any record matches, the whole datagram is forwarded — the records that did not match go with it. Records cannot be removed without re-encoding the export into a different datagram. Send the same stream to BigQuery instead if you need exact filtering.
filter.flowPerRecord: Each flow record is filtered on its own, and only the matching ones become rows.

health.degradedHint: Some messages were rebuilt because no original payload was available.

test.title: Test: {{name}}
test.ok: The test message was handed to the collector. Check that it arrived on the other side.
test.okBigQuery: One test row was written. Query the table to confirm it landed.

warn.noRawCapture: These pollers do not yet supply the original bytes, so their messages are rebuilt even for destinations set to Original: {{pollers}}. They will start supplying them once upgraded.
warn.noFlowRelay: These pollers do not yet relay flow datagrams, so nothing at all is forwarded from the exporters they receive: {{pollers}}. Upgrade them to start the relay.
warn.standby: This core is a standby. Destinations can be edited here, but the active core does the forwarding.

err.duplicate: A destination with that name already exists.
